dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Cardinal is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Cardinal has not acclimatized well to the shelter enviornment despite best efforts to keep him comfortable. He intially presented as fearful and escalated to hard barking and baring teeth in the kennel during attempts to leash him. As his stay progressed, Cardinal became easier to leash and would mostly keep to himself during interactions with handlers. He has recently displayed a concerning level of leash biting when being returned to the kennel. He does not readily release or reliably take treats or toys when trying to redirect him. On two occasions, Cardinal has nearly chewed straight through staff members' leads, and on another occasion, compressed air was used to get him to release, but he did not respond. Medically, Cardinal is apparently healthy.

Cardinal was surrendered to the care center as a stray, and we have no history on his behavior in a home environment. The person who found Cardinal reported that he was gentle, easygoing, and calm for the day that they had him; however, he has not acclimated well to the care center environment, and has allowed only minimal handling since intake. He has shown fearful behavior on being removed from his kennel, escalating to hard barking, growling, and baring teeth. While on walks, he has remained tense and tail tucked. He recently has begun to show an intense level of leash biting after being returned to his kennel. Due to his level of fear, we recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can allow for decompression, provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based), and re-evaluate behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.

A volunteer writes: Cardinal â™¥ï¸ If you spend even a few minutes in the shelter, you can understand why so many dogs, including Cardinal, are scared. To add to that, he was found alone in a park with no collar or leash or owner in sight. His finder spent a day with him looking for his home, and when they couldn't they brought him to the shelter. They said he was gentle and easy going and the intake staff agreed.

And so did we. In spite of his intense initial fear, his reluctance to be handled or assessed, the gentle boy was there when we met him. His little pout and those gorgeous eyes looking up at us show a lost young boy trying to make sense of where he is and who all these new people are. He climbs onto my lap for cuddles while I know he was the same dog who was too scared to have a collar put on him when he arrived. I imagine with more gentleness and stability, the real Cardinal will come out to meet the person who is lucky enough to call him theirs.
dog.name: Cardinal
